status: Lead synthesis for final candidate review; not a validated universal checklist
purpose: Practical questions, not a validated universal assessment instrument or a fixed causal hierarchy

criteria.question: Was the programme usable, relevant and feasible?
criteria.measure_examples: Relevance/acceptability ratings, attendance, completion, task submission, burden, interviews
criteria.can_establish: How participants experienced delivery and whether the planned programme was delivered or completed
criteria.cannot_establish_alone: Learning, changed behaviour, improved follower outcomes

criteria.question: What did participants learn or become able to do?
criteria.measure_examples: Knowledge tests, scored cases, observed simulations; keep confidence/self-rated knowledge separate
criteria.raters: Tests or trained assessors, with participant self-reports identified as such
criteria.timing: Before training, after training, and retention assessment where relevant
criteria.can_establish: Change on the particular task or measure
criteria.cannot_establish_alone: Transfer to an actual workplace or durable impact

criteria.question: Did leadership behaviour change at work?
criteria.measure_examples: Behaviourally specific employee/peer/supervisor ratings, structured observations, work samples or logs
criteria.raters: People exposed to the behaviour and independent observers where feasible
criteria.timing: A genuine pretraining baseline and follow-up after opportunities to apply the skills
criteria.can_establish: Observed or perceived behaviour at stated times and contexts
criteria.cannot_establish_alone: Training caused the change; a generic 360-degree rating is not automatically a validated or unbiased measure

criteria.question: Did followers or teams benefit?
criteria.construct: Relationships, shared identity, team functioning and well-being
criteria.measure_examples: Follower-reported support, team psychological safety, identification, coordination, stress or engagement
criteria.raters: Team members where the claim concerns team experience; leader-only ratings remain leader perceptions
criteria.timing: Baseline and repeated follow-up with stable or documented team membership
criteria.can_establish: The measured experiences or functioning of the sampled followers/teams
criteria.cannot_establish_alone: Objective performance, universal benefit or causation

criteria.question: Did the programme improve outcomes that matter in this setting?
criteria.construct: Service, educational, organizational or clinical outcomes
criteria.measure_examples: Student achievement, retention, service quality, errors, patient-care processes, costs
criteria.raters: Administrative records, independent observation or explicitly identified subjective reports
criteria.timing: Enough follow-up for the proposed mechanism, with relevant baseline or comparison data
criteria.can_establish: Changes or differences in the particular outcome
criteria.cannot_establish_alone: Attribution to training: objective data can still be confounded

criteria.question: Did change last, and were there costs or unintended consequences?
criteria.measure_examples: Repeated outcome measurements, staff turnover, workload, adverse experiences, implementation costs
criteria.raters: Participants, followers and records, chosen for the specific consequence
criteria.timing: Prespecified follow-up and ongoing adverse-event/burden collection
criteria.can_establish: Durability and the observed tradeoffs within the follow-up window
criteria.cannot_establish_alone: No harm when harms were not assessed, or return on investment without both costs and attributable benefits

additional_construct_note: Leader identity, motivation to lead, collective identity and relational leadership may be goals in their own right. Preserve the programme's theory and the instrument's meaning; stronger individual leader identity is not a universal criterion of success.
